course: Convert a Car Engine to an Irrigation Water Pump

lessons.title: L1
lessons.body: In this first lesson, you will learn how to wire a car alternator to charge a 12-volt battery and power your irrigation pump's electrical system. Start by identifying the alternator's terminals: B+ (positive output), D+ (indicator light), and W (tachometer). Use a 10-gauge wire to connect B+ to the battery positive terminal through a 60-amp fuse. Connect the alternator case to a clean metal ground on the engine block. The D+ terminal goes to a 12-volt warning light (2-watt bulb) then to the ignition switch. When the engine runs, the alternator should output 13.8 to 14.4 volts. Check with a multimeter set to DC volts. If voltage is below 13.5, the alternator is weak. For a typical 3-kilowatt pump, you need at least 50 amps from the alternator. In Africa, many used alternators from Toyota or Nissan vehicles work well. Clean all connections with sandpaper and tighten firmly. Use heat shrink tubing on exposed wires to prevent corrosion from dust and humidity. Mount the battery in a wooden box with a lid to protect it from sun and rain. Add a 100-amp circuit breaker between the battery and the pump motor for safety. Test the system by running the engine at 1500 RPM and measuring voltage at the battery. It should rise to 14 volts. If not, check the alternator belt tensionâit should have about 1 cm of play. This basic charging system will keep your battery topped up for long irrigation days.

lessons.title: L2
lessons.body: Now that you have a charging system, you need a battery to store energy for when the engine is off or at low RPM. A deep-cycle lead-acid battery is best for irrigation because it can handle slow discharge. A 12-volt, 100 amp-hour (Ah) battery will run a 1-horsepower (746-watt) pump for about 1.5 hours. For a 2-horsepower pump, use two batteries in parallel (positive to positive, negative to negative) to double capacity. Always use thick cablesâat least 25 square millimeters for battery connections. Install a battery isolator switch so you can disconnect the battery when the pump is not in use. Check battery water level every month; add distilled water only, never tap water. In hot African climates, battery water evaporates faster, so check weekly. Keep terminals clean with a mixture of baking soda and water. Apply petroleum jelly to prevent corrosion. Charge the battery fully before first useâuse a 10-amp charger for 10 hours. Never discharge below 11.8 volts; that damages the battery. Install a voltmeter on your control panel to monitor. For a 24-volt system, connect two 12-volt batteries in series (positive of one to negative of the other). This gives more power for larger pumps. Always wear safety glasses when working with batteriesâthey contain sulfuric acid. If acid touches skin, rinse with plenty of water. Store batteries upright and in a ventilated area. A well-maintained battery lasts 3-5 years.

lessons.title: L3
lessons.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple control panel to start and stop your pump safely. You need a metal or plastic box, a 30-amp toggle switch, a 40-amp relay, a 15-amp fuse, and a push-button start switch. The relay is the keyâit allows a small current from the ignition switch to control the large current to the pump motor. Wire the relay's coil terminals (85 and 86) to the ignition switch and ground. Connect the relay's common terminal (30) to the battery positive through a 40-amp fuse. The normally open terminal (87) goes to the pump motor positive. Ground the pump motor case to the engine block. Use a 12-volt test light to check connections. For automatic control, add a float switch in your water tank. When the tank is full, the float switch opens the relay circuit, stopping the pump. When water level drops, the pump restarts. Float switches are available in most hardware stores in Africa for about $10. Mount the control panel on a wall away from water spray. Label all switches clearly: 'Pump On/Off', 'Battery Voltmeter', 'Fuse'. Use cable glands to seal wire entries against dust and insects. Test the panel by pressing startâyou should hear the relay click and the pump hum. If not, check the fuse and relay. Always disconnect the battery before working on the panel. A neat, well-labeled panel prevents accidents and makes troubleshooting easy.

lessons.title: L4
lessons.body: Your pump motor needs protection from overload, low voltage, and phase loss (for three-phase motors). Start with a thermal overload relay. Set it to 110% of the motor's full load amps (FLA). For a 2.2 kW (3 HP) single-phase motor, FLA is about 13 amps, so set the overload to 14.3 amps. If the motor draws more, the relay trips and cuts power. Next, install a low-voltage disconnect. Use a 12-volt DC voltage monitor relay set to 11.5 volts. When battery voltage drops below 11.5, the relay opens and stops the pump, preventing deep discharge. For three-phase motors, add a phase failure relay to protect against lost phases. In rural Africa, voltage fluctuations are common, so a voltage stabilizer (automatic voltage regulator) is wise. It keeps voltage steady at 230 volts Â±5%. Also install a 30-amp circuit breaker on the AC side if you use an inverter. For DC pumps, use a 50-amp DC breaker. Mount all protection devices in a dust-proof enclosure. Test each device monthly: press the test button on the overload relay; it should trip. Simulate low voltage by disconnecting the battery and checking that the pump stops. Keep a spare fuse and relay on hand. These protections may cost $50-100 but save a $500 motor. In dusty environments, clean relay contacts with contact cleaner every 3 months. Never bypass a protection deviceâit's there for a reason.

lessons.title: L5
lessons.body: To run an AC pump from your 12-volt battery, you need an inverter. Choose a pure sine wave inverter, not modified sine wave, because motors run cooler and last longer. For a 1.5 kW (2 HP) pump, use a 3000-watt inverter to handle starting surge. Connect the inverter directly to the battery with 35 square millimeter cables, keeping the cable length under 1.5 meters. Use a 300-amp fuse on the positive cable. Mount the inverter in a cool, dry placeânot in direct sun. In Africa, ambient temperatures can reach 40Â°C, so ensure good ventilation. If the inverter overheats, it will shut down. For three-phase pumps, you need a three-phase inverter, which is more expensive. Alternatively, use a single-phase motor with a capacitor start. When wiring the inverter, connect the pump's live wire to the inverter's live output, neutral to neutral, and ground to ground. Use a 20-amp AC circuit breaker between inverter and pump. Check inverter output voltage with a multimeterâit should be 220-240 volts AC. If you see less than 200 volts, the battery may be low or cables too thin. Never run the inverter without a ground connection. Test the system by running the pump for 10 minutes and feeling the inverter caseâit should be warm, not hot. If hot, add a small 12-volt fan to blow air over it. Keep the inverter manual for troubleshooting codes. A good inverter costs $200-400 but is essential for AC pumps.

lessons.title: L6
lessons.body: In this final lesson, you will learn to diagnose and fix common electrical problems. Start with a multimeterâa must-have tool. Set it to DC volts to check battery and charging. A fully charged battery reads 12.6 volts; 12.0 volts means 50% charged. If your pump won't start, check these in order: battery voltage, fuse, relay, switch, and motor connections. Use a test light to trace power from battery to pump. If the relay clicks but pump doesn't run, the relay contacts may be burntâreplace it. If the pump hums but doesn't turn, the capacitor may be bad (for AC motors) or the motor is seized. For DC motors, check brushes. A common problem in Africa is corroded connections due to humidity. Clean all terminals with a wire brush and apply dielectric grease. If the alternator isn't charging, check the belt, then the voltage regulator. A quick test: run engine at 2000 RPM and measure battery voltageâshould be 13.8-14.4V. If not, replace the alternator. For intermittent faults, wiggle wires while the pump runs to find loose connections. Keep a logbook of all electrical issues and fixes. Carry spare fuses, relays, and a multimeter in your toolbox. If you smell burning, disconnect battery immediatelyâit's a short circuit. Never work on live circuits. With practice, you'll diagnose most problems in minutes. Remember: 90% of electrical issues are bad connections or dead batteries. Start there.

quiz.q: What is the correct charging voltage range for a 12-volt car alternator?
quiz.explanation: A healthy alternator should output 13.8 to 14.4 volts to properly charge a 12-volt battery.

quiz.q: Which terminal on the alternator connects to the warning light?
quiz.explanation: The D+ terminal is used for the indicator light circuit.

quiz.q: What size fuse should be used between the alternator B+ and battery?
quiz.explanation: A 60-amp fuse protects the charging circuit from overload.

quiz.q: What type of battery is best for irrigation pump systems?
quiz.explanation: Deep-cycle batteries can handle slow, deep discharges typical of pump operation.

quiz.q: How often should you check battery water level in hot African climates?
quiz.explanation: High temperatures cause faster evaporation, so weekly checks are needed.

quiz.q: What should you apply to battery terminals to prevent corrosion?
quiz.explanation: Petroleum jelly seals terminals from air and moisture, preventing corrosion.

quiz.q: What is the minimum voltage a 12V battery should not go below?
quiz.explanation: Discharging below 11.8 volts damages lead-acid batteries.

quiz.q: How do you connect two 12V batteries to get 24 volts?
quiz.explanation: Series connection adds voltages: positive of one to negative of the other.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a relay in the control panel?
options: B) To allow small current to control large current
D) To convert AC to DC
quiz.explanation: A relay uses a small control current to switch a larger power circuit.

quiz.q: Which terminal on a relay is the common terminal?
quiz.explanation: Terminal 30 is the common terminal that receives power.

quiz.q: What device automatically stops the pump when the water tank is full?
quiz.explanation: A float switch opens the circuit when water reaches a set level.

quiz.q: What size fuse should be used for a 30-amp pump circuit?
quiz.explanation: A 40-amp fuse provides protection while allowing normal current.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a thermal overload relay?
options: B) To protect motor from excessive current
C) To convert DC to AC
quiz.explanation: It trips when motor current exceeds a set value, preventing burnout.

quiz.q: At what percentage of full load amps should a thermal overload be set?
quiz.explanation: Setting to 110% allows for normal starting surge without nuisance tripping.

quiz.q: What does a low-voltage disconnect do?
options: B) Stops pump when battery voltage is too low
quiz.explanation: It prevents deep discharge by cutting power below a safe voltage.

quiz.q: What is the recommended voltage for a single-phase AC pump in Africa?
quiz.explanation: Most African countries use 220-240 volts AC for domestic and small industrial equipment.

quiz.q: What type of inverter is best for running AC motors?
quiz.explanation: Pure sine wave inverters produce cleaner power, reducing motor heat and noise.

quiz.q: What size inverter is needed for a 1.5 kW pump?
quiz.explanation: Inverters should be sized at least twice the motor's running watts to handle starting surge.

quiz.q: What is the maximum recommended cable length between battery and inverter?
quiz.explanation: Short cables reduce voltage drop and power loss.

quiz.q: What should you use to protect the inverter from overcurrent?
quiz.explanation: A large fuse like 300-amp is required for high-current inverter circuits.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to check if the pump won't start?
quiz.explanation: Battery voltage is the most common cause and easiest to check.

quiz.q: What does a reading of 12.0 volts on a 12V battery indicate?
quiz.explanation: 12.0 volts corresponds to about 50% state of charge.

quiz.q: If the relay clicks but pump doesn't run, what is likely faulty?
quiz.explanation: Burnt relay contacts can prevent power from reaching the pump.

quiz.q: What should you apply to electrical connections to prevent corrosion?
quiz.explanation: Dielectric grease seals connections from moisture and air.

quiz.q: What should you do if you smell burning from electrical system?
quiz.explanation: Burning smell indicates a short circuit or overheating; disconnect power to prevent fire.

quiz.q: What percentage of electrical issues are due to bad connections or dead batteries?
quiz.explanation: Most electrical problems stem from simple connection or battery issues.

quiz.q: What tool is essential for diagnosing electrical problems?
quiz.explanation: A multimeter measures voltage, current, and resistance for troubleshooting.

quiz.q: How often should you test protection devices like overload relays?
quiz.explanation: Monthly testing ensures they will operate when needed.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a phase failure relay?
options: B) To protect three-phase motors from lost phase
C) To convert DC to AC
quiz.explanation: It disconnects power if one phase is lost, preventing motor damage.

quiz.q: What should you do before working on the control panel?
quiz.explanation: Always disconnect power to avoid electric shock.
